voice-profile.built-from: 50 Robin LinkedIn posts + Nick Saraev/Lenny Rachitsky structural extraction

fingerprint.sentence-length: mixed — 45% short punchy (≤8 words), 43% medium (9-20 words), 12% long. Short sentences punch, medium explain, long are rare
fingerprint.paragraph-length: 1-3 sentences. Lists use → arrows, not bullets. Frequent single-line paragraphs for emphasis
fingerprint.opener-style: statement or observation — NOT a question. Bold factual claim or counterintuitive statement. Patterns: "X just dropped Y", "X has/is Z", "I [personal action]". Only 2/50 posts opened with a question
fingerprint.word-choice: direct and concrete — specific product names (Linear, Claude Code, Postel) over abstractions. Informal contractions (it's, I've, don't). No jargon unless relevant
fingerprint.punctuation: minimal em dashes, occasional ellipsis for drama, parentheticals in 40% of posts. → for lists. Emojis in 24% — 1-2 max, never decorative. No semicolons
fingerprint.first-person: high — 72% use I/my/I've. Default lens: "I built", "I quit", "I tested". Personal experience is the credibility signal
fingerprint.cta-style: soft and conversational — invites reflection or asks for experience. "Would love to hear what's worked", "What's missing?", "Happy building". Never aggressive or sales-y

Chat interfaces are terrible for SaaS

tired of copy-pasting the same context into every ai tool?
I built a fully automated pipeline that turns YouTube videos into LinkedIn posts.
I built a viral tweet browser for X
I tested three agentic frameworks to see if any of them actually make Claude Code better.
This cancellation flow changed how I think about churn...

source.name: nick-saraev
source.post-structure: Bold credibility claim upfront (dollar amount, student count, time period). Then "here's what I found" pivot. Value via numbered list or short paragraphs. Soft close: "I put together a full doc/course" or "reply if you want this".

hook-formulas.formula: I [extraordinary result]. Here is exactly how I did it.
Most people [common approach]. I tried [different approach] and here's what happened.
I [credibility metric]. The real reason is [non-obvious insight].

engagement-tactics.tactic: Lead with specific dollar amounts and percentages as credibility anchors
Long-form value posts that work as carousels
Ends with invitation to get the full resource
Establishes authority before making the ask

source.name: lenny-rachitsky
source.post-structure: Opens with surprising insight or data point. Shares "so what" in 2-3 tight paragraphs. Uses real quotes from named people. Closes with newsletter/podcast connection.

hook-formulas.formula: [Specific data point] — here's what it means for [audience]

engagement-tactics.tactic: Named characters in stories create emotional connection
Data + narrative combo (charts/stats plus story context)
Positions reader as insider getting exclusive insight
Short posts that feel like the summary of a deeper piece
